newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Kabila proposes talks with Mobutu in Lubumbashi.
newsitem.headline: Kabila proposes talks with Mobutu in Lubumbashi.

text.p: Rebel leader Laurent Kabila has proposed he hold talks with President Mobutu Sese Seko in Zaire's rebel-held second city of Lubumbashi, Mobutu's son and spokesman said on Wednesday.

Nzanga Mobutu, who sidestepped a question on whether his father would go to Lubumbashi, told a news conference the veteran strongman still accepted the principle of talks but that the question was where they should be held.
"Mobutu is still agreed to the principle of talks. It's only a question of the venue," he said.

Nzanga Mobutu said his father had told South Africa's Nelson Mandela by telephone on Tuesday that for health reasons he could not respond to his invitation to travel there for talks with Kabila. Mobutu had prostate cancer in Europe last August.

Nzanga Mobutu said Kabila, whose forces took up arms in October and control half of Zaire, had turned down an offer from President Pascal Lissouba of Congo that the talks take place in his capital Brazzaville -- just across the river from Kinshasa. "Kabila said he would not go to Congo but proposed the city of Lubumbashi," he added.
Asked whether Mobutu would go to Lubumbashi, he replied: "That is what Kabila proposed to Mandela. In a few days time, we will know more."
